attempts.summary: Configured node1 (10.100.130.10) as the cluster's internal chrony NTP server, syncing itself from the public pool and serving time to node2 via a firewall-opened ntp service and an allow rule scoped to node2's IP. Configured node2 (10.100.130.11) to sync exclusively from node1 (removed the public pool server line). Verified two-way sync (node2's chronyc sources shows node1 as the current best source; node1's chronyc clients shows node2 polling it). Then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on both nodes: captured pre-restart boot_id and chrony health, issued systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed on both nodes, and re-verified chronyd was active and the client/server sync relationship (node2→node1) was intact after both restarts.
